title: Day 747: Federal Security Cabinet Reports 52 Detained, Meth Labs Disabled Across Six Sinaloa Municipalities
detail: Mexico's federal security cabinet reported that a three-day deployment (August 7–9, 2026) of the Mexican Army, National Guard, Navy (SEMAR), SSPC and State Police across six Sinaloa municipalities — Concordia, Mazatlán, San Ignacio, Navolato, Culiacán, and Ahome — resulted in 52 detentions. Seizures included 46 firearms (41 long guns, 4 handguns, 1 machine gun), 428 magazines, roughly 12,282 rounds of ammunition, 36 tactical vests, 21 ballistic plates, 5 grenades, and 2 improvised explosive devices. In Culiacán, three methamphetamine concentration sites were disabled, with roughly 2,942 liters and 375 kilograms of precursor chemicals secured; officers also seized about 29 kilograms of methamphetamine in Culiacán and marijuana, cocaine and crystal doses in Mazatlán, plus eight vehicles (several reported stolen) and three motorcycles. Two criminal encampments were dismantled in Mazatlán. The cabinet estimated the operation inflicted roughly 62 million pesos in economic damage on organized crime. No casualties were reported.

media.caption: Federal forces detain 52 suspects and disable meth labs across six Sinaloa municipalities, Aug 7–9, 2026

title: Day 747: Gunbattle Interrupts Funeral Mass at Los Mochis Parish as National Guard Pursues Armed Group
detail: A pursuit between National Guard elements and an armed group erupted in the Scally sector of Los Mochis (Ahome municipality) on the night of Sunday, August 9, 2026, as gunfire broke out near the Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de Fátima during a funeral mass. Father Joel Valdez Villegas instructed congregants to remain calm, close the doors, and shelter in place; no one inside the church was injured. The pursuit ended at the intersection of Boulevard Antonio Rosales and Calle Alfonso Cano, where the suspects' vehicle struck a tree. Eight men — all reportedly armed with automatic rifles — were detained; three were injured in the crash and a fourth sustained a gunshot wound. The Sinaloa Public Security Secretariat said the National Guard, with support from an interinstitutional response group, repelled the attack and brought the situation under control.

media.caption: Gunfire near Nuestra Señora de Fátima parish disrupts a funeral mass in Los Mochis, August 9, 2026
